tagline.text: A July festival in Batangas City that brings the Batangas devotional dance, the Subli, out onto the streets

location.label: Location
location.text: Central Batangas City (around City Hall, P. Burgos Street and the Batangas City Sports Coliseum)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Late July (about two weeks, peaking on July 23)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: Watching the events is generally free (transport, meals and lodging extra; check locally)

children.text: The Sublian Festival is Batangas City's signature festival, launched in 1988 to revive the Subli, a traditional devotional dance of Batangas. It runs for about two weeks and peaks on July 23, the city's founding anniversary, with a street dance parade.
The Sublian Festival is a religious and cultural festival held every July in Batangas City, Philippines. It takes its name from the
Subli

, a devotional dance handed down in Batangas. Combining drumbeats, chanted verses and movement, the Subli is closer to a prayer offered by Batangueños to the Holy Cross and the Santo Niño (the Holy Child). The Batangas City official page and English Wikipedia both say the festival lasts about two weeks and culminates on
July 23
, the day the city was founded. It is also said to be listed in the Department of Tourism's calendar of events.

The Subli itself is known to have originated around Alitagtag and Bauan in Batangas. According to local tradition, a cross was found near Alitagtag in 1595 and became the object of devotion in Bauan and Agoncillo. Such origin stories are passed down orally, though, so it is best to keep them separate from the historical record. For a long time the dance was an offering performed to fulfill a vow on the feast of the Holy Cross. Concerned that the dance was fading, Batangas City started the Sublian Festival on July 23, 1988, under then-Mayor Eduardo Dimacuha.

For travelers, the appeal of this festival is that it is not a show staged for tourists; the whole city moves to a single dance. Students, city employees and civic groups take to the streets in Subli hats and traditional dress. It feels more like a neighborhood celebration than a big stage production, which suits anyone who wants to get close to local life. Batangas City is about
105km
from Manila by road, so a day trip is possible, but events start early in the morning, so we recommend staying overnight the day before.

It helps to know a little about what the dance means. The Subli is not just something to watch; it is said to have been danced to fulfill a panata, a vow of thanks or petition. In traditional practice it could be performed on any day except during Lent, at birthdays, graduations or healing requests. The festival carries that meaning into a city event, so if you see dancers bow toward a cross or the Santo Niño, please watch quietly.

blocks.title: Sublian sa Kalye street dance parade

children.text: This is the heart of the festival. The city's description says about a thousand students dance the Subli as they march through the streets, and the parade often lasts an hour or more. In 2025, the street dance and float parade competitions were held on P. Burgos Street on the final day.

Male dancers are said to dance in a stooped posture while striking wooden clappers (kalaste), and female dancers wave and tip their brimmed hats and scarves in salute toward a cross. A drum (tugtugan) and the clappers keep the rhythm, and the group answers a lead singer's verses. Solemn passages alternate with livelier ones.

According to Wikipedia, the Subli has three styles associated with Sinala in Bauan, Pook in Agoncillo and Talumpok in Batangas City. The Talumpok style is considered the oldest, and the festival's street dancing competition is said to be based on it.
The 2025 program listed a court dance competition at

at the Batangas City Sports Coliseum. If the street parade is a lively outdoor event, the coliseum competition is a chance to take in the choreography and costumes calmly on a stage. Times and venues may change from year to year.

At this event you can watch nilupak, a sweet snack made from banana and sweet potato, being prepared and then taste it. Folk singing is part of the program. According to the city's description, it was held at the People's Quadrangle.

Smaller events are added, such as a day celebrating malunggay (moringa), a vegetable known for its health benefits, traditional games, harana serenades, and an evening of song and dance. The lineup can change each year, so check the city's announcements.
In some years a street party was held in the evening in front of City Hall. Shows with celebrities from television networks are also mentioned. It is a relaxed way to unwind after the daytime events.

blocks.title: The Anubing Sublian Festival in Bauan

children.text: Separately from the Batangas City event, one source says Bauan and Alitagtag hold a similarly named festival in early May around the Holy Cross feast. If you want to see the Subli in its home towns, you could confirm the dates separately and plan a May trip.
If you start from Manila, take an early-morning bus to the Batangas City Grand Terminal. If you stayed in the city the night before, skip this step.
In some years this was announced as the start time of the street dance and float parade. Find a spot along the road in front of City Hall, and look for a shaded roadside spot first.
The parade is in full swing. Student groups pass by in different costumes and formations for each section, so take photos and video unhurriedly.
Rest over lunch at a restaurant in town. Try lomi and Barako coffee, local specialties of Batangas, from the local options.
If the court dance competition is held, head to the Batangas City Sports Coliseum. Being indoors, it is a good way to escape the heat.
Look in on the street party in front of City Hall, then head back. Traffic is heavy on the way home, so check the last bus time in advance.
The schedule is based on the 2025 program and changes from year to year. Check the Batangas City announcements before you visit.
Arrive during the festival in the daytime and look around the event sites in town. Seek out food and singing events such as Lupakan at Awitan and get a feel for the atmosphere around City Hall.

Watch the street dance parade from early morning, then spend the day at the coliseum competition or exploring town. If you have time left, you can fill the day by pairing it with the Batangas port area or nearby Taal Heritage Town.
Travel times to nearby places vary greatly with traffic, so check locally.
It is about
105km
by road from Manila to Batangas City. Direct buses to Batangas are said to be available from Manila bus terminals.
Buses usually stop at the Batangas City Grand Terminal (per Wikipedia, around Diversion Road, Alangilan). The ride to Metro Manila is usually 2-3 hours and longer at rush hour. Check before boarding.
On the final day of the festival, road closures can slow entry into the city. Leave early.
Bus companies, terminal locations and fares can change, so check locally.
You can reach Batangas City from Manila by the southern expressway. On festival days, city roads are closed and parking is hard to find.
It is easier to leave the car outside the city center and walk or take a tricycle.
Tricycles and jeepneys run in town. The area around the event sites is within walking distance.
Event routes are closed to vehicles, so check detour routes locally.
The Sublian Festival is most active in late July. It lasts about two weeks and peaks on
July 23
; in 2025 it was held on
July 21–23
. To see the street dance parade, aim for the final day, July 23.

July is the rainy season in the Philippines. The 2025 festival was also reported to have gone ahead amid rain and the southwest monsoon. Bring a raincoat and a waterproof bag, and keep in mind that some of the program may change because of the weather.

items.label: Watching events
items.note: No admission fee is listed on the official page and the street parade is watched from the road; check locally for indoor or paid events

items.label: Bus fare from Manila
items.note: One way, Grand Terminal to Metro Manila, per 2024-25 guides; varies by company and destination

items.label: Lodging
items.note: Rises and fills up early around the final day of the festival

and may vary with local conditions.

For lodging near the events, choose a place in central Batangas City. Rooms fill quickly around the final day, so it is wise to book as soon as your plans are set. Hotel names and rates change over time, so check them on the booking screen.

One food to try is nilupak, available at festival events. It is a snack made by steaming and mashing banana and sweet potato, and it is a traditional Batangas food. Batangas is also known for Barako coffee and lomi (a thick-broth noodle dish), so pick from the local restaurants between events.
The street dance parade tends to start early in the morning. Be ready to move before sunrise.
There is little shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water. In the rainy season, bring a raincoat as well.
Roads along the parade route are closed. When choosing lodging, check that it is within walking distance of City Hall and P. Burgos Street.
Most of the dancers are students, so when taking photos, be considerate and avoid getting too close or disturbing them.
The Subli is a dance with religious meaning. Please be quiet in places where a cross or the Santo Niño is enshrined.
Event schedules and venues change from year to year, so check the latest announcements from the Batangas City government and its tourism office.
If a court dance competition is held in the afternoon after the parade, head to the coliseum. It is a good way to get out of the heat.
Dates and times change from year to year and sources differ on the dates, so be sure to check the latest announcements from Batangas City before you visit.
Watch for pickpockets in the crowded parade area and wear your bag in front.
July is the rainy season, so rain may delay or change the program.
Road closures during the parade cause heavy traffic. Allow extra travel time.
Some sources give July 22 as the date of the Bauan event while others give May 1–3, so they disagree. If you plan to go to Bauan, confirm with the local government.
Prices around the event sites sometimes rise, so ask the price before you buy.
This is the city that hosts the festival. Explore the town center, where the port, City Hall and church are clustered, before or after the events.
A heritage town with Spanish-era buildings and a large basilica. It pairs well as a half-day trip after the events; check travel time locally.
A coastal area famous for diving. It is a good way to continue to the sea after the festival; check travel time locally.
A white-sand beach on the eastern coast of Batangas. You can add it if you have time to spare; check travel time locally.
